observations: Photo 0 shows a person in a grey uniform with 'FABINET' on the chest, standing on a pile of car engines in a warehouse-like setting.
Photo 1 shows a used engine with a black intake manifold and a manual transmission, wrapped in clear plastic.
Photo 2 is a close-up of the same engine as photo 1, showing the '500' marking on the intake manifold.
The engine appears used with some surface rust and wear visible on the aluminum block.
The seller's text claims to sell 'all kinds of Toyota, Lexus, Hyundai, Honda engines and gearbox' and 'direct from Belgium'.
No brand or model is readable on the engine in any photo.

claims.claim: all kinds of Toyota, Lexus, Hyundai, Honda engines and gearbox
claims.evidence: Only one engine is shown in photos 1 and 2; the seller cannot prove they have a wide variety.
No documentation or physical proof of origin is provided.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The engine may not be a Toyota, Lexus, Hyundai, or Honda as claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine's identification plate (usually on the side or front).
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used engine

risks.risk: The engine may be a used unit with unknown history or mechanical condition.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running or a photo of the engine with a handwritten note showing the date of last service.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a used engine with unknown condition

risks.risk: The gearbox may be missing or in poor condition.
risks.proof: A photo of the gearbox next to the engine or a video showing it being tested.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the engine's identification plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the gearbox if included.
Video of the engine running or a photo of the engine with a handwritten note showing the date of last service.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
